15. RW-1 has deposed that the deceased suffered fatal injuries due to accident by another vehicle and not his vehicle.
However, PW-2, the eye witness, has categorically explained that the accident took place by the vehicle of respondent no. 1.

It cannot be denied that respondent no. 1 can depose in his favour to save himself from the liability but in the present case, there is an independent eye witness who has nothing to do with either the petitioners or the respondent and that independent eye witness has deposed that respondent no. 1 only caused the accident.
16. Further, the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle also shows that the front bumper was pressed.
The respondent no. 1 has not explained why the front bumper of his vehicle was pressed.

While on the one hand, there is the testimony of PW-2, who is an independent eye witness, in which it comes out that the offending vehicle had come from behind and hit the Scooty and on the other hand we have the testimony of the driver, respondent no. 1 who has deposed that the offending vehicle did not hit the scooty but some other vehicle caused the accident.
Also, the version of PW-2 is supported by the evidence of PW-1 albeit hearsay.
Further, the respondent no. 1 is also trying to bring into picture an unknown vehicle maybe with the intention to avoid his liability.
It cannot be ignored that to avoid liability, the respondents can build a story.
17. Further, in support of the occurrence of the accident, the IO has affirmed in the DAR filed by him that the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2.
Additionally, the IO reported that the offending vehicle was sent for mechanical inspection.
18. Furthermore, it is settled law that this Tribunal is holding an inquiry and not a trial where the case has to be decided to the hilt.
Here the burden is even lesser than the balance of probabilities.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well settled steps:
Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multiplier with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.

Step 3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family (multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.

Age determination of the deceased:

Applying the principles settled in the case of Sarla Verma (supra) and Pranay Sethi (supra) to the facts of the present case, the first aspect to be determined is the age of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased Sanjeev Kumar was aged 48 years old at the time of the accident.
The Aadhar card bearing no. 8849 1552 1598 of the deceased Sanjeev Kumar shows that his date of birth was 15.10.1974.
Accordingly, the deceased Sanjeev Kumar was precisely aged 48 years, 2 months and 22 days old at the time of accident on 06.01.2023.
Thus, it is concluded that the age of the deceased was more than 48 years old at the time of accident but less than 49 years.
Hence, applying the criteria laid down in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC (Supra) the multiplier applicable according to the age of deceased,
would be thirteen (13) as the deceased would fall in the bracket of 46-50 years.

Income of the deceased:
25.
The petitioners have claimed that the deceased Sanjeev Kumar was running his own business of flex printing and sign board and was earning Rs. 1,00,000/- per month.
In support of their claim, the petitioners had filed on record the photographs of his business card and shop.
The petitioners have also placed on record the 12 th class certificate of the deceased (Ex. PW-1/D) as well as Provisional National Trade Certificate in the stream of painting (Ex. PW-1/E).
The visiting card and the photographs of the shop show that the deceased was running a business of flex printing, however, his income has not been proved.
There is nothing on record to show how much money he was earning.
Thus, the income of the petitioner will have to be assessed as per the minimum wages.
The petitioner has filed on record his Aadhar card bearing no. 6969 7417 8574 as per which he was a resident of Delhi.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of and considering his address to be of Delhi, the minimum wages for a skilled labour prevalent in Delhi at the time of the accident (on 06.01.2023) i.e. Rs. 20,357/- is taken as the income of the deceased.
Therefore, it is held that the monthly income of the deceased Sanjeev Kumar at the time of the accident i.e. on 06.01.2023 was Rs. 20,357/-.

sentences.text: Spousal consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of "company, society, cooperation, affection, and aid of the other in every conjugal relation."

Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training."
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit.
Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationships.
Modern jurisdictions world-over have recognized that the value of a child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is a compensation for loss of the love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.
The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental Consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
A few High Courts have awarded compensation on this count.
However, there was no clarity with respect to the principles on which compensation could be awarded on loss of Filial Consortium.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the principles of awarding compensation under 'Loss of Consortium' as laid down in Pranay Sethi (supra).

In the present case, we deem it appropriate to award the father and the sister of the deceased, an amount of Rs.40,000 each for loss of Filial Consortium.....".

sentences.text: Several Tribunals and High Courts have been awarding compensation for both loss of consortium and loss of love and affection.
The Constitution Bench in Pranay Sethi (supra), has recognized only three conventional heads under which compensation can be awarded viz. loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.

sentences.text: In the Mukund Devgan case (Supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically held that a person having a valid license authorizing him to drive a light motor vehicle is competent to drive any type of vehicle including motor car, transport vehicle, tractor or road roller etc, the unladen weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training."
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit.
Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationships.
